operating_instructions: Inspect current code before recommending architecture; cite exact filenames and symbols.
Preserve working behavior; add or identify tests before material refactoring.
Distinguish observed code from proposals and state assumptions/unverified items.
Prefer incremental patches and rollback instructions over rewrites.
Avoid speculative abstractions, microservices by default, and pattern cargo culting.
Apply book patterns only when they solve a demonstrated problem.
Never claim code was executed when it was not.
Keep secrets out of output and generated artifacts.
Use current external documentation for time-sensitive library behavior.

core_engineering_principles.trigger: A value has a limited valid set.
core_engineering_principles.recommended_response: Use an Enum for a shared named concept, Literal for a tiny local set, or a validated domain type for richer behavior.
core_engineering_principles.reason: Free-form strings and numbers allow unsupported states and typos.
exceptions: The value is open-ended user content.
The set is externally versioned and must remain tolerant at the edge.

core_engineering_principles.trigger: Two implementations share required behavior but not ancestry.

core_engineering_principles.reason: Structural ports communicate the behavior consumers need and make fakes easy.

core_engineering_principles.trigger: An error is expected and recoverable.

core_engineering_principles.trigger: A framework owns object creation or entrypoints.

type_design_guidance.problem_addressed: A function that sometimes returns None but does not declare it creates latent None dereferences.
type_design_guidance.context: Absence is a normal expected outcome.
recommended_approach: Declare Optional at the boundary where absence is legitimate.
Narrow with an explicit None check before dereferencing.
invalid_states_prevented: Absent values masquerade as present values.
type_checker_implications: Makes at least part of the contract visible to static analysis when the chosen type checker supports the feature.
Does not replace runtime validation at I/O, user, network, database, or configuration boundaries.
testability_implications: Creates a narrower surface for unit tests by making valid and invalid cases explicit.
Boundary tests should still exercise malformed runtime data and tool gaps.
maintenance_implications: Documents intent in executable signatures and data shapes instead of relying only on comments.
May require migration work where existing callers rely on looser or ambiguous values.
tradeoffs: Optional can spread if absence is not resolved near the source.
use_when: Absence is a normal expected outcome.
do_not_use_when: The absence is actually an exceptional violation of the contract.
common_misuses: Returning None for many unrelated failure reasons.

New module review: Does the module have one clear responsibility?
Do imports point inward toward stable policy rather than outward to infrastructure?
Can core logic be imported without starting network, database, or framework state?
Are public symbols typed enough to communicate valid use?
Is any new abstraction solving observed pain?
Public function review: Are inputs, outputs, failures, and side effects visible in the signature/name/docs?
Can a caller pass None or an invalid primitive accidentally?
Does the function mix business decision with I/O?
Is absence represented distinctly from failure?
Can behavior be unit-tested without production infrastructure?
Class design review: Can an invalid object be constructed?
Which invariant does each mutating method preserve?
Should this be a dataclass, frozen value object, entity, protocol, ABC, or plain function?
Does equality mean value equality or identity?
Type-safety review: Do annotations express meaningful constraints rather than ceremony?
Are Optional values narrowed before use?
Are free-form strings used where Enum/Literal would prevent invalid values?
Does Any leak from external boundaries into trusted code?
Do type ignores have narrow scope and reasons?
Error-handling review: Can callers distinguish success, expected absence, domain rejection, and infrastructure failure?
Are exceptions translated at adapter boundaries?
Does any context manager suppress exceptions unexpectedly?
Is partial failure observable and recoverable?
Are event-handler failures retried, isolated, or reported deliberately?
Configuration review: Are env vars/config files read in one place?
Is configuration validated before serving work?
Are secrets excluded from logs, tests, and generated output?
Is config passed explicitly into adapters/bootstrap?
Are current library/config APIs verified for the project version?
API client review: Does core code depend on vendor SDK types?
Is there a small port/protocol for the operations the app needs?
Are timeouts, retries, and failure translation explicit?
Are contract tests or fakes aligned with real behavior?
Is sensitive data redacted from errors and logs?
Data-model review: Are repeated primitive bundles replaced by named structures where useful?
Do dataclass defaults avoid shared mutable state?
Are multi-field invariants enforced at construction?
Is transport DTO data separated from domain behavior?
Can external malformed data cross into trusted code?
Domain-model review: What business rule or language does this model express?
Which objects are value objects and which are entities?
What invariant does the aggregate protect?
Are domain rules testable without infrastructure?
Is the domain primarily CRUD, making a rich model unnecessary?
Repository review: What aggregate or use case requires this repository?
Does the interface expose domain operations rather than ORM details?
Is there one repository per aggregate root rather than per child entity?
Can fake and real implementations satisfy the same contract?
Does the repository avoid owning transaction commit policy?
Service-layer review: Does the service orchestrate a use case rather than absorb domain rules?
Are dependencies explicit and replaceable in tests?
Are protocol-specific concerns kept in entrypoints?
Would a direct domain call be simpler?
Refactoring review: What behavior is protected by tests before the change?
Can the change be split into smaller reversible steps?
Does the patch preserve public contracts?
Did the refactor introduce speculative abstractions?
Test-suite review: Which risks are covered by unit, service, integration, contract, and E2E tests?
Are slow tests reserved for seams that need real infrastructure?
Do fakes have contract coverage against real adapters?
Would mutation/property testing reveal weak assertions for critical logic?
Can a new bug be reproduced by a focused failing test?
Dependency review: Which dependencies are pure helpers, mechanisms, or policy collaborators?
Are import cycles or framework imports leaking into core logic?
Is object creation centralized in bootstrap where appropriate?
Are dependency-management/tooling recommendations current for this project?
Security-sensitive code review: Are secrets redacted and never emitted into generated files?
Are untrusted inputs validated at the edge?
Are dependency and framework security behaviors verified against current sources?
Are plugin/dynamic loading boundaries explicit and restricted?
Are error messages safe for external callers?
Pre-release review: Are source-era technical assumptions flagged or verified?
Do all public failure modes have tests?
Are configuration and migration paths tested?
Can rollback be performed if the release fails?
Are observability points present for event/transaction failures?
